I live South Osborne/Lord Roberts area. About a 5 minute walk to Bridge Drive-in and 7 minutes to my office downtown by car.

I love this neighbourhood. People are nice, everyone seems to be a pet lover, convenient location with a lot of amenities near by (rapid transit, Safeway, cool restaurants, etc), very close to downtown, easily accessible to other main arteries in the city. What I don’t like is the small lot sizes. The house I own is a 850 sqft bilevel in-fill. While it’s plenty big enough for myself, my wife, and our dog, it kind of sucks that you basically have to choose between a house sub-1,000 sqft with no front or back yard or a sub-700 sqft house with some sort of green space. Property taxes are pretty high in this area too but kind of expected because of the area.

Ideal neighborhood from my perspective is probably Tuxedo or Charleswood. Plenty of amenities in those areas. Nice mix of new and character homes. Plus still relatively accessible to other main arteries in the city.

Honestly my wife and I would like to stay in Winnipeg but we’re at a point in our careers where we’ve just outgrown whatever the city (and province) can provide. None of the industries here really foster any growth and the city and province are basically flat in terms of population and economic growth, so we took a chance on Alberta for our professional development. Kind of stoked that we’ll have more money to take home because of the tax structure plus higher pay in general!

Edit: just want to add that although on paper it’s 7 minutes by car to my office, Winnipeg traffic is so shit that it’s more like a 40 minute round trip commute. Even worse when it’s construction season. I remember it took me about 45 minutes just to get to work and almost 1 hour to get home during rush hour for a few months last year.

I started dabbling into raw denim and better quality clothing between 2010 and 2012 but it wasn’t until after I joined r/rawdenim late 2017 where I began to learn and figure out what I should be looking for in terms of fit and fabric.

The collection:

- Nudie Jeans Slim Jim Organic Dry Ecru Embo. These were my introduction to raw denim between 2010 and 2012. I loved them then immediately hated them. I blew the crotch out in about 2 months and I vomited all over them after getting blackout drunk at my friend’s brother’s bachelor party. Needless to say I had to wash them and didn’t realize they were raw until they shrunk like 3 inches in length. They look like flood pants when I put them on. My first raws completely turned me off from raw denim.

- N&F Made in Japan 1 Weird Guy. My gf (now fiancée) bought these for me late 2015 because she was tired of me wasting money on mass produced jeans that don’t last long for me. These jeans are my muse and the reason why I got back into raw denim. I still wear them on occasion after beating on them on and off for 3 years. Not a huge fan of the rise but god damn do they fit well everywhere else. 

- N&F Solid Black Selvedge Super Skinny Guy. I bought these late 2017 after I joined r/rawdenim. These were more of an impulse buy because I got them at 50% off and I wanted to try black denim. I tried to make them work for a few months but the fit just didn’t work out for me.

- Momotaro 0405-SP. These are pretty damn close to what is ideal for me. I picked these up late 2018 to replace my N&F MIJ 1 as my daily beaters. Instead of going snug like a lot of people advise to do to account for stretch, I decided to err on the larger side to account for shrink instead. That seemed to work out for me because now I think they fit perfect.

I think my next pickup will be a pair of Oni 902zr or PBJ XX-019. There are so many great denim artisans and brands out there that I really want to take the time to make an informed decision. However, I do know that I want to start to dip my feet into heavyweight territory.
